name: M4: Admin Gmail OAuth provider config + token/scope hardening
description:
MILESTONE 4 — makes the Gmail capability operable by an admin and safe to run for more than one user. Depends on M1; can run in parallel with M2/M3.

Profiles chosen: py_senior (settings model + provider resolution + hardening) and devops (deployment/env var wiring, secret handling, verification readiness).

WHAT TO BUILD:
1. Expose Google as an OAuth provider in global settings: register the provider so get_oauth_provider("google") resolves from the settings file as well as from CODX_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / CODX_GOOGLE_SECRET, and surface it in the existing admin OAuth settings UI (client/src/components/oauth_settings/OAuthSettings.vue) without breaking the GitHub entry.
2. Handling for: token refresh failure, revoked grant, per-user rate limiting, and surfacing GmailAccount.last_error to the owner.
3. Document and implement secret handling: refresh tokens encrypted at rest, client secret only from env/settings, never in logs or git.
4. Deployment doc: how to create the Google Cloud project, which consent-screen user type (Internal vs External) is used, redirect URIs per environment, and what is required before real users outside the org can connect (restricted-scope verification + CASA assessment).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- An admin can configure the Google client id/secret from the admin settings UI, and the user-facing connect flow picks it up without a code change.
- Env-var configuration still wins over the settings file (existing convention preserved).
- A revoked or expired token is detected and shown to the user as a reconnect prompt; the failure is recorded in last_error.
- The deployment doc states plainly what must be done before non-org users can use Gmail read/send.
